does: Scatters flour over food that is already cooking in fat and cooks it for a moment, so that the liquid added next thickens as it simmers.
how: Scatter the flour evenly over the hot, fat-coated food, not in a heap.
Cook it for a moment, stirring, to take away the raw taste.
Add the liquid little by little at first, stirring it smooth.

cues.text: The flour vanishes into a thin paste that coats every piece.
The raw, dusty smell gives way to a faint smell of biscuit.

mistakes.mistake: Tipping the flour in as a heap, which makes lumps that never dissolve.
mistakes.fix: Scatter it from high up, or through a sieve.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the liquid at once, before the flour has cooked.
mistakes.fix: Give it a moment on the heat first.

variant_of.differs: The flour goes onto food already cooking in fat, so that the roux forms around the pieces and is not made on its own.
